blocks.text: ServiceNow is used to set up systems that define, manage, automate, and structure IT services for companies.
There are three ServiceNow connector streams. To learn more, see Zscaler and ServiceNow Deployment Guide.
This article covers the ServiceNow Generic stream. For the ServiceNow Assets and the ServiceNow Users streams, see Configuring the ServiceNow Connector.
To configure the ServiceNow Generic connector, you need the source authentication configuration. Select an authentication method and retrieve the required parameters:

blocks.item: OAuth 2.0
Obtain the following required parameters for the OAuth 2.0 authentication method:
Client ID and Client Secret
Provide the ServiceNow client credentials that were generated using a ServiceNow admin account.
To learn more about creating a client ID and client secret, see Zscaler and ServiceNow Deployment Guide.
Refresh Token and Access Token
To learn more about generating the refresh token and access token for your ServiceNow source, see Zscaler and ServiceNow Deployment Guide.
Tenant ID
The ServiceNow tenant ID.
Verify SSL
Select the Verify SSL checkbox to allow the configuration of a root certificate authority (CA) certificate to trust during the SSL negotiation in the CA certificate field.
User Name Password Client Id Client Secret
Obtain the following required parameters for the Username Password Client Id Client Secret authentication method:
Username and Password
The email and password associated with a ServiceNow Security Admin user and permissions to access the relevant table. To learn more, refer to the ServiceNow documentation.
Client ID and Client Secret
Provide ServiceNow client credentials that were generated using a ServiceNow admin account.
To learn more about creating a client ID and client secret, see Zscaler and ServiceNow Deployment Guide.
Verify SSL
Select the Verify SSL checkbox to allow the configuration of a root certificate authority (CA) certificate to trust during the SSL negotiation in the CA certificate field.
Basic Authentication (Username and Password)
Obtain the following required parameters for the Basic Authentication method:
Username and Password
The email and password associated with a ServiceNow user with the ITIL role or higher and permissions to access the relevant table. To learn more, refer to the ServiceNow documentation.
Verify SSL
Select the Verify SSL checkbox to allow the configuration of a root certificate authority (CA) certificate to trust during the SSL negotiation in the CA certificate field.
Jwt OAuth2
Obtain the following required parameters for the Jwt OAuth2 authentication method:
Client ID and Client Secret
Provide ServiceNow client credentials that were generated using a ServiceNow admin account.
To learn more about creating a client ID and client secret, see Zscaler and ServiceNow Deployment Guide.
Key ID
Provide a Key ID, or Kid, which is generated when you create a new verifier map.
See image.
Subject

This value is used to identify the user in the sys_user table. If the User field in the JWT authentication profile is left as the default, the subject must match the user's email address. If the User field has changed, the Subject must instead match the value in that specified field.
Verify SSL
Select the Verify SSL checkbox to allow the configuration of a root certificate authority (CA) certificate to trust during the SSL negotiation in the CA certificate field.
To learn more, refer to the ServiceNow documentation.

blocks.text: To create the ServiceNow Generic data source in the Agentic Security Operations Platform:

blocks.item: In the Agentic SecOps Platform Admin Portal, go to Configure > Sources.
Click Create.
Search for and select the connector tile from the available data sources.
See image.

blocks.text: After you create the ServiceNow Generic data source, enter the following information in the source setup Retrieval section:

blocks.item: Authentication
To configure authentication:
In the Authentication section, click Create New.
The Service Now Authentication window appears.
In the Service Now Authentication window, enter the information from the Prerequisites section.
See image.
Click Create.
To learn more, see Configuring Authentications and Managing Authentications.
Instance Name

The Instance Name field is the name of the hosted ServiceNow instance. It is found in the URL in the format (e.g., https://[instance-name].service-now.com). For example, if your URL is https://acme.service-now.com/, then the instance name is acme.
Table Name
The name of the table you want to retrieve from ServiceNow.
Query

The query determines whether the search is limited to domains the user is configured to access. Enter true to include the record even if it is in a domain that the ServiceNow user is not configured to access. Enter false to exclude the record if it is in a domain that the ServiceNow user is not configured to access.
Fields Params
The list of fields retrieved from the table.

blocks.text: For complete configuration instructions, see Creating Data Sources.
